MAJOR: Gate-1 context does not embed the latest Gate 1.5 findings + dispositions (CL-006); approval is invalid while any BLOCKER/MAJOR is PENDING — record them or state explicitly that none exist.

Duplicate residency type definitions (standalone Go types vs internal edpsvc types) duplicate the same contract with no single source of truth; a conformance test mitigates but does not remove drift risk. Prefer generating Go types from the JSON schema or sharing one package.

"Identical pass/block from core.packaging.validate and cmd/pfresidency" requires two implementations of the same rules; drift is guaranteed over time. Define which one is authoritative and make the other a thin call-through or clearly derived.
Warn-mode JSONL append (`engineering/residency-gate.jsonl`) has no stated rotation/size bound or concurrency safety; an unbounded append in CI becomes an availability and observability failure.

Alert lead-time / defence-in-depth for blocked builds is unspecified: when the gate flips from warn to block, how does a product team learn before the build fails? No on-startup or pre-merge signal mentioned.
Error-code and report schema stability is asserted but not versioned; no `schema_version`/`report_version` on the JSON report, so downstream consumers cannot evolve safely.
`backup.frequency` "recognized" set is not enumerated in the design; without an explicit closed list the validator's behavior is ambiguous and untestable at the boundary.
MINOR: `retention.legal_hold` is required but its validation semantics (what values, does legal_hold=true relax the days<=policy bound?) are undefined.
No explicit statement that profile file reads are size/schema-bounded or that malformed profile JSON fails closed (only "unknown/missing home" is called out).
Observability is limited to a JSONL event; no metric/counter (blocks vs warns by error code) to measure rollout readiness before flipping to block.
Rollback mentions `gate_mode=warn` or revert, but not what happens to already-emitted manifests or cached `packaging-manifest.json` artifacts during rollback (stale residency sections).
Invariant "allowed_regions includes home_region" is validated in the Go path; ensure core.packaging.validate enforces the same invariant to satisfy the "identical pass/block" AC.
Guardrail 5 (invariants & ordering) and guardrail 9 (tenant isolation / redaction of the residency report) are not addressed in the design text.
NIT: `store-registry.json` ownership registration should name the counsel role explicitly, not just "registered with owners," to satisfy CL-001 route-by-kind.
Affected-files list omits the `engineering/residency-gate.jsonl` artifact and any docs cross-links (ENGINEERING_OPERATING_STANDARD).
The "IN" template default should be justified (or called out as placeholder) so no reviewer mistakes it for a counsel decision.
SUMMARY: Solid, standards-aligned design: fail-closed home_region, Go-first validator, profile-owned policy, warn-then-block rollout, and reversible gate_mode. Top risks are duplicated residency contracts across two implementations (drift), absence of embedded Gate-1.5 findings/dispositions per CL-006, and unbounded/unversioned observability artifacts.
